interpretations.rationale: Present conclusion: in this revision, a follower that accepts a snapshot while its own cached log extends at or beyond the leader's snapshot index is left with an inconsistent log claim and never accepts another log entry from that leader. Basis: installSnapshot updates lastApplied, lastSnapshot and the configurations but never lastLog (raft.go 1930-1977), while getLastEntry prefers the cached log tail whenever lastLogIndex >= lastSnapshotIndex (state.go 160-175). Compaction cannot remove the stale suffix in the non-monotonic store path when TrailingLogs exceeds the log length (snapshot.go 217-252), so the follower's store keeps entries above the snapshot index whose terms differ from the leader's; every AppendEntries prev-log check then either misses below the store's first index or mismatches the stale suffix, the leader's nextIndex is only decremented one step per rejection (replication.go 247-252) until setupAppendEntries reports ErrLogNotFound, and the leader responds by re-shipping the same snapshot (replication.go 296-300, 352-372). Restricted to the measured conditions: three voters, in-memory store, FileSnapshotStore, TrailingLogs=10, an idle cluster plus steady new writes, and a follower restarted on its real on-disk log whose orphan suffix (indexes beyond the leader's snapshot index, lower term) is preserved. Counterevidence considered: the concern that the follower's own election timeout would repair the situation is not observed, because a successful InstallSnapshot refreshes lastContact, so no spurious election fires; and the control refutes 'any stale suffix stalls replication'. Limits: the formal conclusion awaits the controller's retained run of the requested experiment; the reachability of the trigger in production depends on a voter whose log suffix is both longer than the leader's snapshot index and stale in term (a deposed leader or a follower that stored entries from a superseded leader) together with log trimming on the leader; monotonic-store deployments delete the stale suffix instead of keeping it, so their failure mode (entry starvation with the leader's snapshot index at or below the cached claim) still needs its own receipt.

interpretations.rationale: Present conclusion: the phantom log claim produced by the InstallSnapshot path changes how a server decides votes, because requestVote evaluates log completeness with getLastEntry, which prefers the cached claim over the installed snapshot. Source basis: getLastEntry returns (lastLogIndex,lastLogTerm) whenever lastLogIndex >= lastSnapshotIndex (src_get_last_entry, state.go 160-174); requestVote's completeness test rejects only when the voter's last term is greater than the candidate's, or equal with a greater index (src_vote_log_check, raft.go 1725-1748 inside requestVote at 1626-1758); installSnapshot never resets that cached entry (src_install_snapshot_tail, raft.go 1837-1977). Consequence: a voter whose snapshot already contains committed entries in a newer term will still grant a vote to a candidate whose last log entry carries an older term, whenever the cached claim wins the comparison - exactly the case a voter comparing against its snapshot would reject. The scope is bounded rather than established as a safety break: the phantom suffix was never committed (a quorum storing it would have committed it), so its holders were a minority of the configuration that created it, and a leader's snapshot index cannot fall below committed history; a quorum of phantom voters therefore needs a configuration change that turns that minority into a majority of a new configuration. The affected direction is also milder than the phrasing 'stale rejection' suggests: the claim can both reject candidates whose last term equals the claimed term with a lower index and grant candidates whose last term is below the snapshot's term. Limits: this account is source-derived plus local construction feedback (the five-voter probe behaved as predicted: phantom granted, consistent voter rejected, candidate term below the phantom's snapshot term); it has no retained receipt yet, the vote effect is unmeasured in 3-voter configurations, and the configuration-change path that could turn phantom holders into a quorum is not measured at all.
counterevidence: The same root cause in the progress direction was measured to be bounded: starvation ends once a snapshot above the cached claim is published (parent question receipt), so the phantom claim is a transient state within a term, not a permanent log corruption.

A phantom suffix lies beyond the commit index of the term that created it, so its holders are a minority of that configuration; the parent account already argues that a quorum of phantoms then needs a configuration change, which no measurement here supports.
